headline: US tech gives back gains after the ASX breaks its losing streak
paragraphs: The ASX 200 closed Tuesday up 1.8% at 8,726, ending eight straight down sessions. Local technology shares rose 2.8%, catching up with Monday’s US rally. The next US session told a different story: by 5:54 am Wednesday Sydney time the S&P 500 was down 0.60% at 7,193.69, while Nasdaq’s Tuesday intraday reading put the Nasdaq-100 down 1.99% at 26,213.16. Wall Street was still open.

The weakness was more pronounced in tech than in the broad market, even as US consumer confidence improved. The Conference Board’s November index rose to 103.3 from a revised 91.9 in October. The Australian dollar edged back up to 66.45 US cents at 5:15 am Sydney, after the RBA recorded 66.27 US cents at 4 pm Tuesday.

Gold gave up more ground overnight: Kitco’s spot bid was down 2.13% to US$3,556.90 a troy ounce at 5:49 am Sydney. Oil moved the other way: January Brent futures recovered to US$89.88 a barrel, up 0.57%, in a 4:05 am Sydney reading. Those are snapshots, not final prices.
Australia’s October CPI is due at 11:30 am Wednesday. The US October PCE inflation report and the second estimate of third-quarter GDP follow at 12:30 am Thursday, Sydney time.
